author: The Italian Times
title: 47 Years Ago (1979), Italian Musician De André and His Wife Were Kidnapped at Their Sardinian Home
text:
On August 27, 1979, Fabrizio De André and Dori Ghezzi were kidnapped at their home near Tempio Pausania, in northern Sardinia. De André was one of Italy’s most influential singer-songwriters, while Ghezzi was a successful Italian singer. Armed kidnappers took the couple from their estate in the evening. They were then moved to remote areas of the Sardinian interior. The case immediately attracted national attention because of their fame.
The kidnappers belonged to criminal networks commonly known as the Anonima Sequestri. During the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s, these groups carried out numerous ransom kidnappings in Sardinia. De André and Ghezzi remained in captivity for almost four months. They were released in December 1979 after a ransom was paid. Their kidnapping became one of the island’s best-known criminal cases.
The experience influenced De André’s music, particularly the song “Hotel Supramonte,” released in 1981. Despite the trauma, he continued to live in Sardinia and maintained a strong connection with the island. The case remains part of Italy’s cultural and criminal history. It also shows the scale of organized kidnapping in Sardinia during that period. De André’s songs helped preserve the memory of the event for later generations.
